summary: Richard Hugh Robinson specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Alberta, SOAS, and London under Edward Conze, David L. Snellgrove, Arthur Waley, and David Friedman. He taught at Toronto (1954) and became a professor at Wisconsin-Madison in 1961.

Richard Hughes Seager worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD ~1981–1987), later serving as Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College (~1994–2014).
Richard Jay Kohn was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1988, studying under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

Richard K. Payne is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology who studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1990–2020) and taught at the Graduate Theological Union (~1996).

Richard Kieckhefer is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Saint Louis University (~1964–1968) and the University of Texas at Austin (~1968–1972), joining Northwestern University in 1975.

Richard King works in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. After studying at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster under Daniel Mariau, he held posts at Stirling (~1992–2001), Vanderbilt (~2002–2009), and Glasgow (~2010–2013).
Richard M. Jaffe works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held posts at North Carolina State University (~1995–2000) and Duke University (~2000).
Richard Mahoney is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA at the University of Canterbury by 2002 under the supervision of Paul Harrison and held a post there in 2001.

Richard Morris was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Battersea Training College (~1852–1854) and held posts at King's College School (~1869–1890) and the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875).

Richard P. Boyle studied at the University of Washington and under traditional teacher Joshu Sasaki. He taught at the University of California, Los Angeles, and held an affiliation with the University of New Mexico attested in 2015.

Richard P. Hayes studied Sanskrit and Indian studies at Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal, Shoryu Katsura, and T. Venkatacharya. He taught at Toronto, Leiden, McGill University (attested 1997–2009), and the University of New Mexico (attested 2011–2016).
Richard Peter Hottelet worked in Buddhist studies, studying under Narayan Hemandas Samtani and holding a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison attested in 1971.

Richard Pischel was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Breslau, Kiel, Halle-Wittenberg, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1908), alongside the Prussian Academy of Sciences.
Richard Polenberg was a historian who studied at Columbia University (~1959–1964) and held a faculty post at Cornell University from ~1966 to 2011.

Richard Rorty was a philosopher who studied at the University of Chicago (~1946–1952) and Yale University (~1952–1956). He held academic posts at Wellesley College (~1958–1961), Princeton University (attested 1987), and Stanford University (~1998–2005).

Richard Salomon is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He held a post as professor at the University of Washington (attested 1998–2017) and was a guest researcher at Soka University in 2007.
Richard Schmidt was an Indologist who studied under Ernst Mehliß and completed his studies at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1888–1893).

Richard W. Lariviere studied Indology at Iowa and Pennsylvania. He served at the University of Texas at Austin (~1982–2006; Dean ~1999–2006), Kansas (~2006–2009), Oregon (~2009–2011), and as President of the Field Museum (~2012–2020).
Richard Wilhelm was a Sinologist who studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium. He held posts at Peking University (~1922–1924) and Goethe University Frankfurt (~1924–1930).

Richard von Garbe was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Rudolf von Roth and Bhagavata Acharya. He later succeeded Roth at the University of Tübingen, serving as chairholder from 1895 to 1927.
